newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London rebounded in the afternoon on firmer New York values but prices finished off their peaks on overhead origin selling. December closed $15 higher at $1,503 a tonne. November's premium to January widened to touch a high of $62 before closing at $58, up from Monday's finish of $49.

As anticipated, arabica futures in New York were able to bounce in response to yesterday's large reduction in certified coffee stocks. The figures released after the market closed on Monday, showed a sharp fall of 10,433 60-kg bags on the week to 31,669 bags, the lowest level in at least 10 years.

The US stock data, coming at the start of the 1996/97 South American harvest, underpinned prices and could boost the CSCE December's premium to the distant months. However, the upside potential seems limited because new crop coffee should be available to supplement supplies.

BRAZIL - According to John Wolthers of Icato/Sumatra, Brazil's 1997/98 coffee crop is not likely to be a bumper harvest as is expected by some traders. The trees this year recuperated as best they could from the high stress caused by two frosts and a drought in 1995, with the 1996/97 harvest resulting in a high production cycle of about 26 million 60-kg bags, it was said.
It was added that the Brazilian coffee crop has a two-year 'on-off' cycle, when every other year is a larger crop. Producers have already said they expect the coming crop to be below that of 1996/97.

BELGIUM - Belgium imported 162,044 bags of coffee in May 1996, 11 per cent less than was imported the same month the previous year. That brought total imports since the beginning of 1996 up to 803,200 bags, 8.4 per cent less than was imported the same period in 1995. Total imports in calendar year 1995 dropped by 7.5 per cent to 2.068 million bags.
Major suppliers of green coffee in January/May 1996 were Ivory Coast (40,000 vs 28,200 bags), Brazil (67,600 vs 91,800 bags), Colombia (34,700 vs 28,600 bags) and India (34,300 vs 2,600 bags).

The country exported 578,500 bags of coffee in January/May 1996, 15 per cent more than was exported the same period in 1995. Total exports in calendar year 1995 dropped by 7 per cent to 1.204 million bags.

SOUTH KOREA - South Korea imported 425,300 bags of coffee in January/May 1996, 16 per cent less than was imported the same period in 1995. Total imports in calendar year 1995 dropped by 7.5 per cent to 1.084 million bags. Major suppliers of green coffee in January/May 1996 were Honduras (55,600 vs 40,800 bags), Indonesia (88,800 vs 40,200 bags) and Vietnam (56,500 vs 116,700 bags).
